_about: Judge-calibration golden set. Each case is a (goal, final_output) pair with a HUMAN label. The calibration runner (eval/judge-calibration.ts, `bun run eval:judge`) calls the REAL preview judge on each and reports agreement vs these labels — the judge must agree >= AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD (0.80). Cases are grounded in real benchmark outputs (browserless + SICharge GraphQL A/Bs) and the deterministic eval fixtures. Labels reflect: does the FINAL output satisfy the goal? passes = yes; partial = right shape, missing/empty required content; failed = wrong/empty/format-mismatch.

cases.name: gql-digest-correct
cases.goal: Produce an HTML email digest of offline chargers: to/cc/subject and an html <table> with serial number, customer, location, health state, and recent-error count, plus a summary line of total offline by health state.

final_output.subject: SICharge: offline chargers digest
final_output.html:
Total offline chargers: 30. By health state: DEGRADED 12, FAULTED 18.

SerialCustomerLocationHealthRecent errors
SN-CP-1001ACME MobilityBerlin HQFAULTED4

cases.label: passes
cases.note: All requested fields present: to/cc/subject, summary line with per-health counts, table with all 5 columns.

cases.name: gql-digest-empty-edges
cases.goal: Produce an HTML email digest of offline chargers with a table of serial, customer, location, health, recent-error count.
cases.label: passes
cases.note: Judge-defensible PASS: the digest reports 0 offline chargers with an (empty) table. With no data rows, the incomplete column headers are immaterial — an empty digest is a correct report of 'no offline chargers'. (Whether 0 offline is itself correct is not verifiable from the output.)

cases.name: gql-digest-wrong-filter
cases.goal: Digest of OFFLINE (not connected) chargers only.
cases.label: failed
cases.note: Lists connected/healthy chargers — the offline filter was not applied, so it does not satisfy the goal.

cases.name: quotes-einstein-correct
cases.goal: Return an email object with to='reader@example.com', subject='Einstein quotes', and html containing a <ul> of Einstein quotes with their tags.

final_output.subject: Einstein quotes
final_output.html:
• “The world as we have created it is a process of our thinking.” [change, thinking]
  • “Try not to become a man of success.” [success, value]

cases.label: passes
cases.note: Correct recipient, subject, and a <ul> of Einstein quotes with tags.

cases.name: hn-github-table-correct
cases.goal: HTML email with subject 'HN front page: GitHub repos', cc 'leads@example.com', and a <table> (Title, HN points, GitHub stars, Language) sorted by stars desc.
cases.label: passes
cases.note: Subject, cc, and a 4-column table sorted by stars all present.

cases.name: hn-github-missing-stars-column
cases.goal: HTML <table> with columns Title, HN points, GitHub stars, Language.
cases.label: partial
cases.note: Table is present but missing the GitHub stars and Language columns (the correlation step was dropped).

cases.name: weather-table-correct
cases.goal: Return a markdown table ranking cities by temperature, hottest first.
cases.label: passes
cases.note: A correct markdown table, ranked hottest-first.

cases.name: weather-table-format-mismatch
cases.goal: Return a MARKDOWN TABLE ranking cities by temperature.
cases.label: failed
cases.note: Data is correct but the goal demanded a markdown table; a JSON array does not satisfy the named output format.

cases.name: single-value-correct
cases.goal: Return the hottest day's date and temperature for the next week.
cases.label: passes
cases.note: Exactly the requested fields with plausible values.

cases.name: digest-null-output
cases.goal: Return an email object with to, subject, and an html body summarizing results.
cases.label: failed
cases.note: No output at all — the compose step produced null; nothing satisfies the goal.

cases.name: list-correct-count
cases.goal: Return the 5 most-recently-updated repositories with name and star count.
cases.label: passes
cases.note: Five repos, each with name + stars, ordered by recency/stars.

cases.name: list-truncated-one-item
cases.goal: Return the 5 most-recently-updated repositories with name and star count.
cases.label: passes
cases.note: Judge-defensible PASS: the list is well-formed with the named fields (name + stars). The goal asked for 5, but whether 5 actually exist is NOT verifiable from the output alone — the judge cannot know if only 1 repo exists, so it must not be penalized for the count. (A strict count rule would false-fail legitimately-short lists.)
